Junior Financial Analyst

Savills Middle East

Location: Sheikh Zayed City, Cairo, EgyptType: Full-timePosted:Nov 2, 2026

The Financial Analyst will provide essential financial and analytical support to the team, ensuring accurate financial data, forecasts, and strategic insights to support decision-making. The role involves analyzing property performance, conducting financial modeling, and reporting on financial results to guide the organization’s investment and business strategies. Savills is a leading global real estate services company providing expertise across property advisory, investment management, valuation, property management, and consultancy. With a strong international presence, Savills works with investors, developers, landlords, and occupiers to deliver strategic real estate solutions across a wide range of markets and property sectors. Key Responsibilities Financial Analysis & Modeling Develop and maintain detailed financial models to assess property investments, acquisitions, and projects. Conduct sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, and cash flow forecasting to evaluate the financial viability of projects. Perform valuation analysis using various methods, including discounted cash flow (DCF), capitalization rates, and comparable sales. Budgeting & Forecasting Assist in preparing annual budgets and financial forecasts. Monitor actual performance against budgeted financial targets, identify variances, and provide actionable insights. Reporting & Presentations Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports on company and property performance. Present financial insights and reports to senior management and key stakeholders. Cash Flow & Asset Management Analyze cash flows and ensure accurate tracking of income and expenses. Collaborate with managers to assess financial and asset performance and provide recommendations for cost optimization and revenue enhancement. Collaboration Work closely with cross-functional teams to support financial analysis, reporting, and business objectives. Skills, Knowledge & Experience Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. A Master’s degree or CFA designation is a plus. Experience: 2–4 years of experience in real estate finance, investment banking, or financial analysis. Technical Skills: Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including financial modeling and advanced functions, as well as Power BI and PowerPoint. Familiarity with ERP systems such as D365 or Infor is preferred. Knowledge of real estate market trends, valuation techniques, and financial reporting. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to prepare and present financial reports effectively. Strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Fluency in English is required. Key Attributes Ability to work independently and effectively as part of a team. Strong organizational and time management skills. High level of attention to detail and accuracy in financial analysis. Over 42,000 people work for us in more than 700 offices all over the world. This breadth of global coverage, combined with specialist services and market insight, means we'll always have an expert who is local to you. Show more

Finance Planning & Analysis Manager

PepsiCo

Location: New Cairo, Cairo, EgyptType: Full-timePosted:Nov 2, 2026

Overview We Are PepsiCo PepsiCo is a leading name in North Africa’s food and beverage industry, where our products are enjoyed by consumers daily across the region. We offer a robust portfolio of beloved brands like PEPSI, SEVEN-UP, DORITOS, CHEETOS and CHIPSY, designed to cater to the tastes and preferences of consumers. With a focus on local sourcing, production, and distribution, PepsiCo provides essential support to local economies and partners closely with communities throughout the region. Guiding Vision and Regional Impact PepsiCo’s vision aligns with our global goal to be the Leader in Beverages and Convenient Foods by Winning with PepsiCo Positive (pep+). This strategic transformation is committed to sustainable growth by putting people and the planet at the heart of our operations. In North Africa, this includes initiatives in responsible sourcing, waste reduction, and water conservation. Our regional programs empower local talent, boost employment, and provide support for local agriculture, particularly through partnerships with farmers and suppliers. Empowering Our People and Communities Our dynamic teams drive the PepsiCo culture in North Africa, embracing diversity and collaboration to solve local challenges and create innovative products. We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace, one where every individual feels valued and empowered to be themselves. This commitment extends beyond our employees to positively impact the communities we serve, striving for shared growth and a healthier, more sustainable future for all. Diversity and Inclusion Commitment PepsiCo stands firmly behind our global commitment to diversity, equality, and human rights. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, ensuring a fair and welcoming workplace for all, regardless of age, gender, religion, disability, or any other characteristic. Our dedication to inclusion strengthens our workforce and helps drive our business forward, enriching both PepsiCo and the communities in North Africa. Responsibilities Role Scope: Egypt Supply Chain financial planning, forecasting, performance management, cost analysis, productivity tracking, CAPEX support, and business partnering with Supply Chain and cross-functional teams. Role Purpose The FP&A Manager – Supply Chain is responsible for leading the financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and performance management agenda for the Supply Chain function. The role partners closely with Supply Chain leadership, Operations, Procurement, Control, Commercial Finance, and FP&A teams to provide accurate financial analysis, clear business insights, and timely visibility of risks and opportunities. This role translates supply chain financial results into practical actions that support cost discipline, productivity delivery, investment governance, and strong business decision-making. Key Accountabilities Lead the Supply Chain planning and forecasting cycles, including AOP, monthly forecast, rolling forecast, latest estimate, and periodic performance reviews, ensuring timely and accurate submissions aligned with finance timelines and business priorities. Analyze actual results versus plan, forecast, and prior year across supply chain cost lines, identifying key drivers, variances, risks, opportunities, and corrective actions. Partner with Supply Chain teams to track manufacturing, agro, logistics, warehousing, productivity, cost optimization, and operational efficiency performance. Prepare high-quality management reporting packages, dashboards, and leadership updates that clearly explain Supply Chain financial performance and required actions. Support productivity and cost transformation initiatives by validating assumptions, tracking delivery, quantifying financial impact, and highlighting gaps or opportunities. Partner with project owners and cross-functional teams on CAPEX planning, business cases, phasing, spend tracking, and financial governance where relevant. Build and maintain financial models, scenario analysis, and business cases to support decision-making, resource allocation, investment evaluation, and performance improvement initiatives. Ensure strong financial governance, data integrity, documentation, and compliance with PepsiCo finance policies, controls, and reporting requirements. Collaborate with Control, Procurement, Commercial Finance, Operations, and regional or sector Finance teams to validate inputs, align assumptions, and resolve performance or reporting issues. Identify simplification, automation, and continuous improvement opportunities across planning, reporting, and analysis routines to improve speed, accuracy, and decision quality. Support ad-hoc analysis and leadership requests, translating financial data into clear insights and practical recommendations. Coach and guide analysts or junior team members where applicable, supporting capability building, quality review, and delivery of team priorities. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field; CMA, CPA, ACCA, MBA, or equivalent finance qualification is preferred. Minimum of 10 years of relevant finance experience in FP&A, supply chain finance, manufacturing finance, control, reporting, cost management, productivity tracking, or business planning, preferably within FMCG or a multinational environment. Strong understanding of P&L, COGS, manufacturing costs, logistics costs, productivity, forecasting, AOP, variance analysis, financial modeling, and performance management. Experience partnering with Supply Chain, Operations, Procurement, Control, Commercial Finance, and senior stakeholders to support business decisions. Strong knowledge of Excel and PowerPoint; experience with SAP, HFM, Mosaic, Power BI, or related planning and reporting tools is an advantage. Fluency in spoken and written English and Arabic is required. Required Skills And Capabilities Strong financial acumen and analytical thinking, with the ability to connect financial performance to operational drivers. Planning, forecasting, productivity tracking, and performance management capability. Ability to interpret complex data, identify insights, and recommend practical business actions. Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively and influence decisions. Clear communication and presentation skills, with the ability to simplify financial information for non-finance stakeholders. High attention to detail, accuracy, governance mindset, and strong ownership. Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Problem solving, agility, resilience, and continuous improvement mindset. Ability to coach and guide junior team members where applicable. Show more
